ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: making it up after the fight

texts.li: {A_nameDef} went looking for {B_nameDef} after their fight, and the two of them talked it through until neither was angry any more.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the fight between them had been stupid, and {B_nameDef} said it had been, and that was the end of it.
After their fight, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} both started to say sorry at the same moment, and then laughed about that.
{A_nameDef} held out a hand to {B_nameDef}, still sore from their fight, and after a long moment {B_nameDef} shook it.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} sat down beside {B_nameDef} and said, the way {A_possessive} people end a quarrel, that the fight was buried and wouldn't be dug up.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} there was no shame in their fight and less in ending it, and gave {B_objective} {A_possessive} hand on it.
[industrial] {A_nameDef} found {B_nameDef} and said {A_pronoun}'d rather have {B_objective} on {A_possessive} side than a black eye to remember {B_objective} by, and {B_nameDef} agreed.
[spacer] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that two people on one small world can't afford a feud, and their fight was over.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: made it up after a fight

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: a joke too far

texts.li: {A_nameDef} wouldn't let a joke at {B_nameDef}'s expense go, and by the fourth time {B_nameDef} wasn't laughing.
{A_nameDef} gave {B_nameDef} a new nickname and kept using it after {B_nameDef} asked {A_objective} to stop.
{A_nameDef} told the story of {B_nameDef}'s last mistake, then told it again with more in it.
{A_nameDef} kept a joke about {B_nameDef} going long after it was funny, and {B_nameDef} walked off in the middle of it.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} acted out {B_nameDef} chasing a hare and losing it, and did it again when the first one got a laugh.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} made up a rhyme about {B_nameDef} and kept singing it, a verse longer each time.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} kept doing {B_nameDef}'s voice at every chance, and wouldn't stop when asked.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: a joke that went too far

texts.li: {B_nameDef} stopped {A_nameDef} to say it plainly: {B_pronoun} owes {A_objective} for patching {B_objective} up under fire, and means to pay it.
{B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} {B_pronoun} still thinks about the fight, and who came for {B_objective} while it was going on.
{B_nameDef} saved {A_nameDef} the first helping and the warm seat, and said it was the least {B_pronoun} owed after the fight.
[tribal] {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that where {B_pronoun} was raised a life saved is a life owed, and {B_pronoun} keeps to that.
[medieval] {B_nameDef} swore to {A_nameDef}, half in jest and half not, to stand at {A_possessive} side in the next fight as {A_pronoun} stood at {B_possessive}.
[industrial] {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the next drink is on {B_objective}, and every one after it, for what {A_pronoun} did in the fight.
[spacer] {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} {B_pronoun} keeps a list of what {B_pronoun} owes, and {A_nameDef} is at the top of it.
{A_nameDef} saw {B_nameDef} favoring {B_possessive} bad side while they were {WORK}, and took the heavy end without a word.
{B_nameDef}'s old injury was playing up while they were {WORK}, and {A_nameDef} took over the worst of it.
{A_nameDef} noticed {B_nameDef} wincing and swapped places with {B_objective}, so {B_nameDef} had the light work for a while.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} to rest the old hurt and leave the lifting to younger bones, whatever age those bones were.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} to mind that old injury before it put {B_objective} back on the sick list, and took the load.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were {WORK} side by side, and without a word it became a race.
{A_nameDef} saw how fast {B_nameDef} was going and sped up, and {B_nameDef} saw that and sped up too.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} kept {WORK} long past the point of sense, each waiting for the other to stop first.
{A_nameDef} pointed out a spot {B_nameDef} had missed, and {B_nameDef} pointed out two of {A_nameDef}'s, and they went on {WORK} faster than ever.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were {WORK} within earshot of each other, and each one counted the other's pace under {A_possessive} breath.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were {WORK} side by side and talked the whole way through it.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} found a rhythm, {WORK} together, and the work went quicker for it.
{A_nameDef} passed {B_nameDef} what {B_pronoun} needed before {B_pronoun} asked for it, the way people do who have worked together a long time.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} a long story while they were {WORK}, and {B_nameDef} made {A_objective} start it again from the middle.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} started an old work song while they were {WORK}, and {B_nameDef} came in on the second verse.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about music the whole time they were {WORK}, and agreed on none of it.
{B_nameDef} brought {A_nameDef} the {THING} {B_pronoun} had just finished, and {A_nameDef} turned it over a long time before saying it was good.
{A_nameDef} looked over {B_nameDef}'s new {THING}, found the one flaw in it, and then said {B_pronoun} had done well.
{A_nameDef} held up {B_nameDef}'s {THING} to the light and said {A_pronoun} had nothing left to teach {B_objective} about this one.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that the {THING} was the work of a sure hand, and that the old ones would have known it for one.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the {THING} was a journeyman's work, and meant it as the praise it was.
[industrial] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {A_pronoun} couldn't have made a better {THING} at {B_possessive} stage, and {A_pronoun} had tried.
[spacer] {A_nameDef} said no fabricator would have put the care into the {THING} that {B_nameDef} had, and the care showed.
{A_nameDef} picked up {B_nameDef}'s new {THING} and didn't want to put it down.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} how {B_pronoun} made the {THING}, and listened to the whole answer.
{A_nameDef} ran a thumb along {B_nameDef}'s {THING} and asked how long it took, and {B_nameDef} tried not to look pleased.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} said {B_nameDef}'s {THING} would still be in use when both of them were long gone.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} said {B_nameDef}'s {THING} was better than anything the traders bring, and {A_pronoun} would know.
{A_nameDef} looked at {B_nameDef}'s new {THING} for a long time and said only that the edges were rough.
{B_nameDef}'s {THING} was all the talk, and {A_nameDef} found somewhere else to be.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the {THING} was fine, for a first try, which it wasn't.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} who had really made the {THING}, and didn't seem to be joking.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: a quiet word after a loss

texts.li: {A_nameDef} stopped beside {B_nameDef} and said the name of the one they lost, and they stood a while without saying anything else.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} one small thing {A_pronoun} remembered about the dead, and {B_nameDef} told {A_objective} another.
{A_nameDef} didn't ask {B_nameDef} how {B_pronoun} was, only sat with {B_objective} long enough for {B_nameDef} to say it.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the dead walk with those who remember them, and {B_nameDef} remembers well.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} said a few plain words to {B_nameDef} about the one buried, and that the grave would be kept.
[industrial] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} there's no right way to take a death, and {B_pronoun} was doing it as well as anyone.
[spacer] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the dead had chosen this place as much as any of them, and wouldn't have wanted the work to stop.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: a quiet word after a loss

texts.li: {A_nameDef} asked to see {B_nameDef}'s fresh hurt, winced at it, and wanted the whole story.
{A_nameDef} checked how {B_nameDef}'s hurt was mending and told {B_objective} to stop picking at it.
{A_nameDef} made {B_nameDef} tell how {B_pronoun} got hurt, and kept saying it could have been much worse.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} a scar is a story the body keeps, and {B_nameDef} would have a good one.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} looked at {B_nameDef}'s hurt the way a farrier looks at a hoof, and pronounced it clean.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} to keep the dressing dry and come to {A_objective} if it went red.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef}, loudly, whether {B_pronoun} had ever tried looking where {B_pronoun} was going.
{A_nameDef} acted out how {B_nameDef} got hurt, with the yelp, and {B_nameDef} didn't laugh.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {B_pronoun} had been lucky, and then listed all the ways {B_pronoun} had been stupid.
{B_nameDef} listened to {A_nameDef} complain about the {ILLNESS}, then told {A_objective} what {B_pronoun} did for it in {B_possessive} day.
{B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} {B_pronoun} had the {ILLNESS} twice when {B_pronoun} was young, and both times it went in the end.
[tribal] {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} to chew willow bark for the {ILLNESS} and sleep near the fire, as {B_possessive} people always did.
[medieval] {B_nameDef} swore by a mustard poultice for the {ILLNESS}, and described it to {A_nameDef} in more detail than {A_pronoun} wanted.
[industrial] {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} that for the {ILLNESS} there was nothing to beat bed, broth and leaving it alone.
[spacer] {B_nameDef} told {A_nameDef} the medicine would see to the {ILLNESS}, and the rest was rest and patience, which no medicine makes.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} who to ask for what around here, and who never to ask.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} which jobs nobody wants and which ones are worth asking for.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the things the colony never says out loud, starting with who doesn't get on with whom.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} named the landmarks around the camp for {B_nameDef}, and the stories that go with them.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the colony's ways: who sits where, who eats first, and what not to say to whom.
[industrial] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} how the work gets shared out here, and how to get out of the worst of it.
[spacer] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that out here nobody cares where you came from, and then asked {B_objective} where {B_pronoun} came from.
{B_nameDef} was glaring at {B_possessive} plate, and {A_nameDef} sat across from {B_objective} and talked {B_objective} out of it.
{A_nameDef} kept up a stream of small talk over the meal until {B_nameDef} cracked a smile.
{A_nameDef} ate beside {B_nameDef} and asked nothing, which was what {B_nameDef} needed.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} every bit of the day's news over the meal, and {B_nameDef} stopped scowling halfway through.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} sat down with {B_nameDef} at the meal and complained about the food until {B_nameDef} joined in.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} got caught out in the rain, gave up trying to stay dry, and stood in it laughing.
The rain came down on {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} out in the open, and neither of them would be the first to run for cover.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the rain would stop any minute now, and kept saying it until they were both soaked through.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} held a wide leaf over {B_nameDef}'s head in the rain, which kept neither of them dry.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} held {A_possessive} jacket over {B_nameDef}'s head in the rain, which kept neither of them dry.
{A_nameDef} got {B_nameDef} in the back of the neck with a snowball, and it was war from then on.
{B_nameDef} was halfway through a sentence when {A_nameDef}'s snowball arrived, and the sentence was never finished.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} threw snow at each other until neither could feel their hands, and called it a draw.
{A_nameDef} built a wall of snow to hide behind, and {B_nameDef} walked round it and knocked {A_objective} into it.
{A_nameDef} pulled {B_nameDef} into the shade for a breather, out of the worst of the heat.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {B_pronoun} was red as a beet, and made {B_objective} stop and drink before going on.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} made {B_nameDef} stop work and drink from the water skin before the heat got {B_objective}.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} made {B_nameDef} stop for a long drink of water and stood over {B_objective} until {B_pronoun} finished it.
[industrial] {A_nameDef} passed {B_nameDef} a canteen in the heat and wouldn't take it back until it was half empty.
[spacer] {A_nameDef} pushed a water flask into {B_nameDef}'s hands and told {B_objective} heatstroke would slow the work far more than a drink would.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: stamping in the cold

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} stood out in the bitter cold stamping their feet, each telling the other it wasn't so bad.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {B_possessive} nose had gone white, and {B_nameDef} said {A_nameDef}'s had gone blue.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} compared which of their fingers they could still feel, and {B_nameDef} won by one.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} blew on their hands in the cold and talked about the fire they'd sit at later.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the warmest place {A_pronoun} had ever been, in detail, to make the cold worse.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: stamped their feet in the cold together

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} worked the field side by side before the cold, and talked about what the winter would need.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} were bringing in the crop together and kept guessing how much the stores would hold this year.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} worked the plants together and thanked the earth for each basket, the old way.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} raced the frost together in the field, and {A_nameDef} said it was a good year's work.
[!lowtech] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} worked the field together and worked out, between them, how many days of food each row was.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} took different sides in the neighbors' war, and it got loud.
{A_nameDef} said one side of the neighbors' war had it coming, and {B_nameDef} said that was exactly what the other side says.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} whose side {B_pronoun} would be on in the neighbors' war, and didn't like the answer.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} wondered who they knew in the towns at war, and whether they were all right.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {A_pronoun} kept thinking of the farms between the two armies, and {B_nameDef} had been thinking the same.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the neighbors' war, and agreed the ones who pay for it are never the ones who start it.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: the households on the road

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the households on the road, and where they would sleep tonight.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about the time {A_pronoun} had to leave a home behind, and {B_nameDef} listened to the end.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} counted what the colony could spare for the families walking past, and came out at different numbers.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: talked about the households on the road

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: a joke about the dry town

texts.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the colony could get rich selling beer over the dry town's wall, and {B_nameDef} started working out the price.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} raised imaginary cups to the dry town's thirsty young people.
{A_nameDef} wondered aloud to {B_nameDef} how long the dry town's law would last, and they bet on it.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: a joke about the dry town

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: what we would build

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} heard about the neighbors' great work and argued happily over what the colony would build if it could.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the colony could raise something just as grand one day, and {B_nameDef} asked with whose hands.
[tribal] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the neighbors' longhouse, and planned one of their own twice its length.
[medieval] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the neighbors' new hall, and planned a tower for the colony that would look down on it.
[industrial] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the neighbors' dam, and planned where the colony's would go.
[spacer] {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the neighbors' signal tower, and what they would say if the colony had one.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: planned what the colony would build

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.label: the summer that never came

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about the summer that never came, and what the colony has put by against the winter.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {A_pronoun} had never known a summer this cold, and {B_nameDef} said {B_pronoun} had, once, and told {A_objective} about it.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went through what grows in the cold, and what the colony might plant instead.

ColonyCouncil.SocialEventDef.note: talked about the summer that never came
